items.t: Duke Energy stock: Florida plans four new solar sites
sum: Duke Energy Florida filed plans on Tuesday, November 10, with the Florida Public Service Commission for four new solar energy sites. Duke Energy said the projects are intended to add 300 megawatts of clean generation and deliver an estimated 1 billion US dollars in customer savings over their operating lives.

The planned sites are Nova Renewable Energy Center, Bull Creek Renewable Energy Center, Hogeye Renewable Energy Center and Wewahootee Renewable Energy Center. They are located in Orange and Sumter counties, with construction scheduled to begin between January and May 2027.

The company expects the projects to enter service between February and June 2028. Duke Energy Florida said fuel-cost savings and production tax credits are expected to support the customer benefit cited in the announcement.

The project plan gives investors a further view of Duke Energy's renewable-generation pipeline and its expected capital deployment in Florida. The announcement concerns planned facilities; construction and regulatory milestones remain the next operating steps.
Duke Energy stock traded at 117.08 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 10:51 CET on Saturday, November 14.

Duke Energy stock: SEC filing details January subsidiary merger
sum: Duke Energy's planned subsidiary reorganization has gained a more detailed legal outline. In a Form 8-K reporting an event from November 9, the utility said it expects to transfer its ownership interest in Duke Energy Carolinas to Progress Energy before combining Duke Energy Progress with Duke Energy Carolinas on January 1, 2027.

The filing from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission says Duke Energy Progress will merge into Duke Energy Carolinas, which will remain the surviving entity. Lenders consented to the combination through an amendment to the group's credit agreement.

The filing provides additional detail on the sequence of the internal steps. It describes a contribution of Duke Energy Carolinas to Progress Energy, followed immediately by the merger of Duke Energy Progress into Duke Energy Carolinas. The transaction concerns wholly owned subsidiaries and is not a merger of Duke Energy Corporation itself.

The planned completion remains January 1, 2027. For investors, the development is primarily an execution milestone tied to the utility's corporate and financing structure; the filing does not announce a purchase price or a new earnings target for the parent company.

Duke Energy stock traded at 116.25 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 16:13 CET on Friday, November 13, 2026. The quote provides the latest trading context as investors assess the company's restructuring plans and broader utility outlook.

- Duke Energy’s 3.4% yield makes it the cheapest route, about $46,500 less than Con Edison, but its dividend took the biggest share of earnings: 67% of fiscal 2025 normalized EPS.

items.t: Duke Energy stock: guidance floor rises after Q3 beat
sum: Duke Energy's third-quarter update, reported on Thursday, November 5, showed stronger earnings and a higher floor for its full-year outlook. The company posted adjusted earnings per share of 1.99 US dollars, up from 1.81 US dollars a year earlier, according to Ad Hoc News.

Duke Energy stock traded at 114.00 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 16:14 CET on Monday, November 9, 2026. That was 1.30% below the 115.50-euro quote cited in the company's latest report published earlier the same day at 13:48 CET. The comparison is separate from a Xetra daily move.

For the quarter ended September 30, net income increased to 1.56 billion US dollars from 1.42 billion US dollars in the prior-year period. Revenue rose 6.6% to 9.1 billion US dollars, while the result exceeded the cited FactSet consensus of 1.86 US dollars per share.

Duke Energy now expects 2026 adjusted earnings of 6.70 to 6.80 US dollars per share, compared with the previous range of 6.55 to 6.80 US dollars. Management left the upper boundary unchanged and expects to finish the year near the top of the revised range.

The utility also reaffirmed its target for adjusted earnings growth of 5% to 7% through 2030 and expects to reach the upper half of that range from 2028. Infrastructure investment recovery and stronger electricity and natural-gas demand supported the quarter, while depreciation, interest expense, minority-interest effects and a higher effective tax rate were offsets.

Duke Energy prices $1.75B equity unit offering at $50 per unit
sum: Duke Energy completed a $1.75 billion public offering of 35 million equity units priced at $50 each. The units combine senior notes with stock purchase contracts, offering a 7.75% annual distribution. Proceeds will be used to redeem long-dated junior subordinated debentures and repay commercial paper.
*this image is generated using AI for illustrative purposes only.

Duke Energy Corporation has priced a public offering of 35 million equity units at $50 per unit, raising an aggregate stated amount of $1.75 billion. The offering is expected to close on August 13, 2026. Each Corporate Unit consists of a contract to purchase Duke Energy common stock in the future, combined with two 1/40 undivided beneficial ownership interests in the company’s remarketable senior notes: one series due 2032 and another due 2036, both carrying a coupon rate of 4.85% and a principal amount of $1,000 per note.

The structure provides investors with total annual distributions at a rate of 7.75%, derived from interest payments on the senior notes and contract adjustment payments. Under the associated stock purchase contracts, holders are required to purchase a variable number of Duke Energy shares no later than August 1, 2029. The reference price for these contracts is set at $121.1827 per share, reflecting the closing price on August 10, 2026. The minimum settlement rate is 0.3301 shares, based on a threshold appreciation price of $151.4693 (a 25% premium over the reference price), while the maximum settlement rate is 0.4126 shares.

Duke Energy intends to list the Corporate Units on The New York Stock Exchange, with trading expected to commence within 30 days of issuance. The underwriters hold an option to purchase up to 5 million additional units, representing $250 million in aggregate stated amount, to cover over-allotments. If fully exercised, the total raised could reach approximately $1.965 billion after deducting underwriting discounts but before offering expenses.

The net proceeds, estimated at approximately $1,719 million, will be used to redeem $500 million of the company’s 3.25% Junior Subordinated Debentures due 2082. Additional funds will repay outstanding commercial paper and support general corporate purposes.

sum: Duke Energy reported stronger third-quarter results on Thursday, November 5, 2026, and raised the lower end of its full-year adjusted earnings outlook. The utility said reported and adjusted earnings per share reached USD 1.99 for the quarter ended September 30, compared with USD 1.81 a year earlier, according to the company's Form 8-K release.
Duke Energy stock traded at EUR 116.75 on Lang & Schwarz at 14:18 CET on Thursday, November 5, 2026. Investors can follow the real-time quote of Duke Energy stock.

The company narrowed its 2026 adjusted earnings-per-share guidance to USD 6.70 to USD 6.80 from a previous range of USD 6.55 to USD 6.80. Management said strong performance through the first three quarters positioned Duke Energy to deliver near the upper end of the revised range. It also reaffirmed a long-term adjusted EPS growth target of 5% to 7% through 2030, based on the 2025 guidance midpoint of USD 6.30.

Management does not provide a long-term forecast for reported GAAP earnings per share. The company said the quarterly improvement reflected recovery of infrastructure investments in growing service territories and favorable weather. Higher depreciation on the expanding asset base, minority-interest effects, higher interest expense and a higher effective tax rate partly offset those gains.

Electric Utilities and Infrastructure generated segment income of USD 1.817 billion, up from USD 1.658 billion in the third quarter of 2025. The improvement included a USD 0.20 contribution per share from the segment, with rate-case impacts, customer volume and weather supporting the result. Gas Utilities and Infrastructure reported a USD 19 million loss, an improvement from a USD 26 million loss a year earlier.

Group revenue increased to USD 9.104 billion from USD 8.542 billion. Net income available to common shareholders was USD 1.551 billion, compared with USD 1.407 billion in the prior-year quarter. The reported effective tax rate rose to 15.3% from 10.8%, mainly because of lower amortization of excess deferred income taxes.
Duke Energy is executing a generation expansion aimed at adding 16 gigawatts of capacity by 2031.

Comstock Holding Companies, Inc. (Nasdaq: CHCI) ("Comstock" or the "Company"), a leading real estate company specializing in the development, acquisition, operation, and management of mixed-use, transit-oriented properties and data center developments, today announced that it has entered into a purchase agreement to acquire The Ascher, a 672-unit Class A multifamily property located in Uptown Charlotte, North Carolina (the "Purchase Agreement"). Upon closing, which is expected in the fourth quarter of 2026, The Ascher will join Comstock's growing portfolio of premier residential communities.

Opened in 2016, The Ascher includes two 24-story residential towers offering studio, 1, 2, and 3-bedroom floor plans, approximately 13,000 square feet of ground-floor retail, and a controlled-access parking garage with more than 900 spaces. The two buildings share a 6th-floor rooftop courtyard that includes a regulation tennis and pickleball court, a bocce court, a putting green, covered lounge seating with cafe tables, fire pits, grilling area, fenced-in dog parks, and an on-site pet spa. Each tower also includes its own private rooftop pool and sky terrace with panoramic city views, fitness center, resident clubhouse and lounge, and grilling area. In-unit amenities include floor-to-ceiling windows, private balconies, well-equipped kitchens, and washers/dryers.
